attempts.summary: On node1 (Alpine 3.23), created the `datauser` account, provisioned a dedicated 300MB loopback ext4 filesystem (native ext4 quota feature enabled via tune2fs) mounted at /srv/data (persisted in /etc/fstab with usrquota,grpquota), owned by datauser, and applied a filesystem-enforced user quota of 100MB (102400 1K-blocks, soft=hard) for datauser via setquota. Verified enforcement: writes up to ~99MB succeed, writes beyond 100MB fail at the kernel/filesystem level with "Quota exceeded" (ENOSPC-style EDQUOT), independent of any application logic. Added /etc/local.d/srv-data-quota.start (enabled in the default OpenRC runlevel) to guarantee quotaon runs at boot. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, quota state, mount, and a data marker file; issued a native reboot; polled until node1 was reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed (412576a1... -> 11f48b77...); confirmed the /srv/data mount, quota accounting/enforcement, and marker file all recovered automatically without any manual intervention; re-ran the over-quota write test post-restart and confirmed it still fails as expected.
